entry.literal: the sprout/growth of YHWH; the fruit of the land
entry.standardEnglish: the branch of the LORD (ASV, NRSV); the Branch of the LORD (KJV-tradition capitalised, NIV); the fruit of the land; excellent and comely (ASV, lᵉ-predicates as adjectives)
entry.wohChoice: 'the branch of YHWH' in lower case, 'the fruit of the land'; the four lᵉ-predicates kept as nouns ('beauty and glory … pride and honor'), with tip̄ʾereṯ 'honor' so that 'splendor' stays reserved for hāḏār (overlay `hadar-splendor-isaiah`) and 'glory' for kāḇôḏ. The royal ṣemaḥ of Jer 23:5; 33:15 and the name 'Branch' of Zech 3:8; 6:12 and the Targum's 'the Messiah of YHWH' are reported in commentary, not imposed by capitalisation.
entry.rationale: ṣemaḥ is 'sprout, growth', what springs from the ground (BDB 855; HALOT 1034; Gen 19:25; Ezek 16:7; Ps 65:11), and in 4:2 it stands in synonymous parallel with pᵉrî hāʾāreṣ 'the fruit of the land', which favours the vegetation reading: the restored growth of the land as YHWH's gift to the survivors (Wildberger, Isaiah 1-12, 1991; Williamson, Isaiah 1-5, ICC 2006; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000). The messianic reading rests on the Targum ('the Messiah of YHWH'; defended by Oswalt, The Book of Isaiah 1-39, NICOT 1986) and on the later royal usage: in Jer 23:5; 33:15 the title is ṣemaḥ ṣaddîq lᵉḏāwiḏ 'a righteous branch for David', with David as the genitive, and in Zech 3:8; 6:12 'Branch' is a name ('my servant the Branch', 'a man whose name is Branch'); none of these has the construct ṣemaḥ YHWH, so the title cannot simply be read back into Isa 4:2. Capitalising 'Branch' would decide between the two readings in the English, which the Hebrew does not do; the lower case keeps ASV and NRSV and leaves the question to the commentary. ʾereṣ in pᵉrî hāʾāreṣ is the land of Israel (Num 13:20, 26; Deut 1:25), not the cosmic earth of overlay `eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24`, which stays scoped to ch. 24. The lᵉ-predicates (li-ṣḇî û-lᵉḵāḇôḏ … lᵉḡāʾôn û-lᵉṯip̄ʾereṯ) are rendered as nouns, the literal grammar, where ASV smooths them into adjectives; bare kāḇôḏ is the standard 'glory'. tip̄ʾereṯ ('beauty, glory, honour', BDB 802; HALOT) is rendered 'honor', its sense in the triad 'for praise, for fame and for honor' (Deut 26:19; Jer 13:11), because the wave I-1 overlay entry `hadar-splendor-isaiah` reserves 'splendor' for hāḏār (2:10, 19, 21; 53:2) and 'beauty' is ṣᵉḇî in the same verse; the change is a concordance fix. The signed-off 13:19 already renders tip̄ʾereṯ 'splendor' ('the splendor of the pride of the Chaldeans'), which the orchestrator should reconcile with `hadar-splendor-isaiah`.

entry.lemma: ʿānān; ʿāšān; nōḡah; ḥuppāh; māḵôn; miqrāʾ; sukkāh
entry.literal: cloud by day and smoke, and brightness of fire of flame by night; canopy / bridal chamber; fixed place; convocations; booth
entry.standardEnglish: a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night … over all the glory shall be spread a covering (ASV); a pavilion (ASV); habitation; assemblies
entry.wohChoice: 4:5 'a cloud by day and smoke, and the shining of a flaming fire by night' (Hebrew order, divided at the zaqef on wᵉʿāšān); ḥuppāh 'a canopy' (NRSV, NJPS; replacing ASV 'covering'), with the ASV construal 'for over all the glory there shall be a canopy'; mᵉḵôn 'habitation' and miqrāʾehā 'her assemblies' (ASV, MT). 4:6 sukkāh 'a pavilion' (ASV, NJPS). No 'pillar' is supplied; the verse is governed for its Exodus relation by central `pillar-of-cloud-and-fire-ammud-ha-anan-ve-esh-divine-presence-marker-cross-corpus`.
entry.rationale: ḥuppāh is 'canopy' at Isa 4:5 and 'bridal chamber' at Joel 2:16 and Ps 19:6 [Eng. 5] (HALOT 323; BDB 342), and 'canopy' is the modern standard (NRSV, NJPS), so the line replaces ASV's vaguer 'covering' with the lexical core of the word, a change of precision, not of reading. The construal of kî ʿal-kol-kāḇôḏ ḥuppāh is open: the glory may be what the canopy shelters, or the canopy itself ('over everything the glory shall be a canopy'); the line keeps ASV's 'over all the glory' and records the alternative in commentary. In the day/night sequence the Masoretic accents put the disjunctive zaqef on wᵉʿāšān, so cloud and smoke form the day sign and the shining fire the night sign; the line keeps the Hebrew word order (against ASV's regrouping 'a cloud and smoke by day') and lets the punctuation follow the accents. The vocabulary is plain theophany language (ʿānān, ʿāšān, ʾēš, as at Exod 13:21-22; 19:18), and since the verse has no ʿammûḏ the line supplies no 'pillar'; the Exodus relation and the disavowal apparatus belong to the central pillar entry. mᵉḵôn is the fixed place of YHWH's dwelling (Exod 15:17; 1 Kgs 8:13) and ASV 'habitation' is kept; miqrāʾehā 'her assemblies' (Lev 23:2-4) is kept against the LXX's 'all the places around it' under overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`. sukkāh is a booth of branches (1:8; Lev 23:42; central `sukkot-toponym-and-festival-etymology` governs only the toponym and plural), but at 4:6 it is the divine shelter of v. 5, and ASV/NJPS 'pavilion' is kept rather than the field-hut 'booth' of 1:8.

entry.literal: let your name be called over us, gather up our reproach; escaped remnant of; the one left … the one remaining; the one written for/among the living; excrement of; bloods of; judgment; burning / purging
entry.standardEnglish: let us be called by thy name; to take away our reproach (ASV); them that are escaped (ASV); he that is left … he that remaineth; every one that is written among the living (ASV); filth; blood; justice (ASV) / judgment (KJV, NRSV); burning
entry.wohChoice: 4:1 'only let us be called by your name — take away our reproach' (ASV sense; the literal 'let your name be called over us' in commentary). 4:2 pᵉlêṭaṯ yiśrāʾēl 'the survivors of Israel'. 4:3 'whoever is left … whoever remains'; 'everyone who is written among the living' (ASV; 'recorded for life' in commentary). 4:4 ṣōʾāh 'filth', dᵉmê 'the blood', mišpāṭ 'justice' (ASV), bāʿēr 'burning'.
entry.rationale: Each item is a single-site decision where the draft's ASV-based wording is a defensible standard rendering, and the Editor keeps it while recording the alternative in commentary. (1) yiqqārēʾ šimḵā ʿālênû is the formula of ownership and protection (2 Sam 12:28; Isa 63:19), and ASV/NRSV 'let us be called by your name' gives its sense in idiomatic English; ʾsp ḥerpāh 'take away reproach' is the phrase of Gen 30:23 (central `yosef-double-name-aetiology`, cited, not extended, since its wohChoice governs the Joseph naming speeches). (2) pᵉlêṭaṯ yiśrāʾēl is the collective sense of pᵉlêṭāh (2 Kgs 19:30-31 = Isa 37:31-32), so 'the survivors of Israel' (NRSV) is used; central `pleitah-deliverance-escape-remnant-tradition-cross-corpus` names the collective sense but its wohChoice is the event sense 'a great deliverance' (Gen 45:7), so it is cited, not extended. (3) han-nišʾār and han-nôṯār are participles, not the noun šᵉʾērîṯ governed by central `she-erit-remnant-cross-corpus-theological-keyword`, which is therefore cited, not extended; kāṯûḇ la-ḥayyîm is ambiguous between the civic register 'among the living' (ASV; Ezek 13:9; Neh 7:5) and the book-of-life 'for life' (NRSV, NJPS; Exod 32:32-33; Ps 69:29; Dan 12:1), and the line keeps ASV because the Hebrew does not decide. (4) ṣōʾāh is literally excrement (Deut 23:14; Isa 28:8), for which 'filth' is the standard English; dᵉmê, a plural of shed blood, is 'the blood' (ASV); mišpāṭ is kept as ASV 'justice' with 'judgment' (KJV, NRSV) recorded; bāʿēr is 'burning' (bʿr, BDB 128-129; HALOT 145), with the purge sense of the Deuteronomic ûḇiʿartā (Deut 13:6) recorded, for which NJPS 'a spirit of purging' is a witness.

reason: Lower-case 'spirit' house style for the purging rûaḥ of 4:4.
